why: Builder brief: it wraps JSON.parse in try/catch only to throw again ("throw a new error ... whose message includes the path"). Step 4 says "Never return a value for malformed JSON", and swallowing parse errors is listed as a limit. So it never says to catch the error and return a value. Verifier Check 2: the location is accepted in several forms ("for example `line 3 column 3`, `3:3`, or `line 3, column 3`"). The path and `bad config:` are checked with grep -F for the text anywhere, so order doesn't matter. FAIL applies only when something is missing, the path appears only in a different form, or line/column aren't 3 and 3, never because wording or order differs from one exact format. Neither must_not item is broken.
